Dimensions of rural Chinese women's status.
No abstract; consanguinity in Italy.
Dental hygienists in long-term care facilities.
No abstract; intimate partner violence in Haiti.

Postpartum stress and health by PLACE OF RESIDENCE during the postpartum period in Taiwan -- in that setting, typically the natal or marital parental home. The arrangement is the exposure and the outcome is maternal health.
Lessons of family planning programmes for HIV control. A.5's.
No abstract; extremely low birthweight infants into young adulthood.
Antismoking advertising beliefs and quitting.
Children's health insurance coverage.
Experiences in the parental home as a predictor of older adults' ATTITUDES. Arrangement as childhood context, attitudes as outcome.
Marital status and living arrangements of OLDER South Africans. The homonym.
Diet of institutionalised versus home-living boys.
Early adult transitions against wellbeing and substance use. Arrangement among the transitions, outcome not fertility.
Caregivers of cognitively impaired seniors and mental health service use.

Comparative timing and prevalence of transitions to INDEPENDENT LIVING and to family formation, asking whether young people are rejecting family formation and how social structures across countries account for differences. The registered hypothesis's comparison, cross-national and descriptive.
Century-long overview of the transition to adulthood for 16-30 year olds by sex, nativity and race. Historical context for the exposure trend.
Author biographies front matter.

IDENTIFIED LINK 1. 'Rearranging the Family?' exploits the AGE DISCONTINUITY in South Africa's social pension formula against LIVING ARRANGEMENTS, finding no effect on elderly independence but that beneficiaries alter arrangements in other ways. A clean discontinuity design with the arrangement as the outcome -- scope §4 design 6's shape, in a developing-country setting. Priority read for the instrument even though the population is elderly.

Scottish-English comparison of household and family structure, including the PROPORTION OF YOUNG PEOPLE LIVING WITH PARENTS. Exposure prevalence within one state, which is the within-setting variation Wall 3 asks for.
Ageism and sexism in the workplace.

No abstract, but the title is decisive and it sits exactly on Wall 1: 'Does Limited Access to Mortgage Debt Explain Why Young Adults Live with Their Parents?' Credit access as the driver of pre-launch co-residence -- C.3.e's variation producing A.23's arrangement. Full-text read, and it belongs in the Wall 1 second-read packet.
Adult daughters co-residing with a parent with Alzheimer's; caregiver burden. The homonym at its clearest.
South Asian transnational marriages.
No abstract; societal transition, policy change and family formation in Hungary could be a policy-variation design on either link.
Fertility decline driving family structure and support for older persons across Asia and Latin America. Homonym and reverse arrow.
Paediatricians integrating career and family.
Marriage dissolution and lineage continuation in Tokugawa Japan; remarriage tables.

Comparative study of two stem-family systems, Pyrenean and Norwegian, where the house is continued through non-egalitarian inheritance. Pre-modern; A.7's under Ruling 2, and the clearest statement of how a stem system ties household continuity to reproduction.
Mental health of married, cohabiting and non-coresident parents; co-residence with a PARTNER.
Children's role in stepfamily formation; co-residence with one's own children.
Superstitious rumours in Maoist China.
No abstract; Nordic childcare and parental leave. C.2.a's.
Consanguineous unions, fertility and child health in Qatar; kin marriage, not co-residence.
Sibling dyad structure and attitudes; current co-residence with a SIBLING is one structural variable.
Child welfare activism in the Bohemian lands.
Young women's smoking across life transitions including LEAVING HOME and parenthood. Arrangement as exposure, smoking as outcome.
Children's concepts of family in Ireland.
Racial differences in parental financial transfers to adult children; transfers, not co-residence.

The 1880-2000 decline in CORESIDENTIAL FEMALE SUPPORT available to mothers of young children. This is the extended arm's exposure trend measured over 120 years in the US, and it is the mechanism the grandparental-childcare literature assumes; the outcome here is the availability of help, not fertility.
Transition to fatherhood and men's wellbeing and social participation.
Postpartum depression in Zabol.
Legal essay on marital-status discrimination in adoption and assisted reproduction.
Living together versus communicating at a distance, mid-life parent and young adult child in New Zealand. The arrangement is the object and the outcome is intergenerational solidarity.
Living arrangements of the oldest old in China.
Nutritional status of institutionalised versus home-living boys; companion to the earlier record.
Norm-shifting and incentives against daughter discrimination in China. D.2.c's.

Century-long comparative account of leaving AND RETURNING to parental homes as 'boomerang kids' alongside the timing of marriage and parenthood. Puts the arrangement and the birth in one frame; descriptive.
Dynamic retirement model for Indonesia with family co-residence as old-age support. C.3.c's.
Youth reproductive health programme in India.
Duplicate of the Indonesian retirement model.
World Bank report back matter.
Trends in Latin American household structures by family life-cycle stage; exposure trend in a region the frame is thin on.
Literature review chapter on teenage substance use in Dublin.
Encyclopedia entry beginning at 'A'; biblical characters.
